title: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint for macOS — Deployment & Onboarding via Intune
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (macOS + Microsoft Intune/Entra; configuration/identity/security work, live-fleet care).
White-label; Apple/Microsoft console internals authored click-by-click from public docs; anything uncertain flagged, not invented.
hook: Onboard every Mac to Defender the way macOS actually requires
problem: Deploying Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on macOS is not a one-click app push — it needs the system-extension, full-disk-access, network-filter, and background-services profiles delivered before onboarding, or it silently fails. This solution deploys and onboards MDE for macOS through Microsoft Intune correctly — the required config profiles, the onboarding package, and health validation — deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the MDE-for-macOS deployment model: system extensions, full-disk access (PPPC/TCC), network filter, background service management, and the onboarding blob delivered via Intune.
Requirements Guide — prerequisites (MDE licensing, Intune enrollment, the required config profiles, onboarding package, a pilot) with how to verify/implement each.

Implementation Guide — exact ordered steps to deploy the named system-extension / full-disk-access / network-filter profiles FIRST, then the onboarding profile, assign to a pilot, validate MDE health, and expand.
5 PowerShell scripts — MDE-readiness discovery, per-device onboarding + profile validation, an MDE health/coverage report, safe remediation of missing profiles, and a target-group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (profiles applied, onboarded, healthy) plus Best Practices for extension approval order.
short: Deploy and onboard Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on macOS via Intune correctly — system-extension, full-disk-access, and network-filter profiles before the onboarding blob — pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
